title: How Corey Haines builds a SaaS marketing budget: two reverse-engineered methods
summary: Corey Haines argues that project-by-project budgeting is lazy and that most SaaS startups don't know how marketing spend relates to revenue growth. He offers two methods: set a budget as 5-40% of annual revenue, or start from a revenue goal and work back to a budget using ARPC, CAC and retention, with buffers built in.

principles.text: Budgeting project by project slows progress and keeps you thinking too small.
principles.quote: Budgeting on a project-by-project basis slows down progress, discourages experimentation, and boxes you into thinking too small and conservatively.

principles.text: Pick a marketing budget between 5% and 40% of ARR, matched to how ambitious your goals are and how much capital you have.
principles.quote: Simply slide the scale up and down from 5% to 40% until you agree on how aggressive you want to be and how much money you have to deploy from the start.

principles.text: Calculate CAC as a blended number: salaries, ads, tools and content, divided by new customers in the last year.
principles.quote: CAC should be blended to include salaries, advertising costs, technology, content creation costs... everything related to acquiring new customers.

principles.text: Overestimate CAC rather than underestimate it, since CAC is the main dependency and errors cascade into missed revenue goals.
principles.quote: It’s far better to overestimate CAC than to underestimate.

principles.text: When given a revenue goal, reverse-engineer the budget: new customers needed times CAC, divided by annual retention rate.
principles.quote: The budget is essentially determined by reverse-engineering the relationship between the goal and the customer acquisition unit economics.

principles.text: Add 10-20% on top of the budget as an experimental budget so you can be wrong and still hit the goal.
principles.quote: As a good rule of thumb, tack on an additional 10-20% to your marketing budget and label it “experimental budget.”
